The test image shows a corn leaf with distinct yellow/pale streaks running parallel to the veins — no pustules, spots, or lesions with borders. This suggests a systemic/viral or vascular disease. Top candidates: Maize_Streak_Virus, Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus, Stewart_S_Disease, Maize_Chlorotic_Dwarf_Virus.

Now viewing one reference from each of 4 candidates:

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Corn leaf with fine pale yellow/white streaks running parallel to the veins along the full leaf length. Background tissue still mostly green. No pustules, lesions with margins, or necrotic spots.

- **Maize_Streak_Virus ref**: More intense orange-yellow streaking — same pattern but more advanced stage. Test image matches as an earlier/milder infection.
- **Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus ref**: Subtle mottling on a young leaf — less well-defined streaking than test image.
- **Stewart_S_Disease ref**: Wider, bleached/tan irregular streaks — fewer but more prominent bleached patches vs. the many fine streaks in test image.
- **Maize_Chlorotic_Dwarf_Virus ref**: Blotchy yellow patches scattered on leaf — clearly different pattern.

The fine, closely-spaced pale yellow streaks running parallel to the veins across the full leaf is most characteristic of **Maize_Streak_Virus**, which produces yellow to white streaks along the leaf. The test image likely represents an early/moderate stage before the streaks become the intense orange-yellow seen in the reference.
